carbon_policy_signal.item: France-Germany Industrial Accelerator Act disputes carbon cost allocation to heavy industry; ETS regulatory clarity TBD, affecting hydrogen arbitrage incentives.
carbon_policy_signal.why_it_matters: Outcome determines whether carbon cost pass-through to power or hydrogen shifts marginal dispatch incentives; ETS forward pricing and decarbonization investment pace hinge on ruling.

freshness_caveat: Coal metric stale as of 26 Dec 2025 (249 days old); current fuel-switch economics and merit-order dispatch unconfirmed. GB Power, TTF, EUA, and Storage all current (0–2 days old).
risk_flags: Strait of Hormuz disruption would spike crude >USD 100/bbl, lifting EU power marginal fuel cost 5–8 EUR/MWh and forcing coal back into merit order.
EU storage at 65.1% full, 16.8 pp below seasonal — winter 2026-27 refill pace will set H2 power curve; any LNG supply shock now cascades.
GB power at 165.91 EUR/MWh (97th pctile) vs EU power unavailable — GB-DE spread widening historically; supply-side constraint or demand divergence warrants investigation.
Coal data stale since 26 Dec 2025 (249 days old); current dispatch economics unconfirmed — cannot assess fuel-switch regime with confidence.

base.summary: Hormuz risk priced into TTF; Libya ramp offsets. Storage refill gradual; GB premium persists.

downside.summary: Hormuz tensions ease; Libya ramp accelerates. EU power supply slack emerges; storage refill normalizes.

upside.summary: Hormuz shipping incident or Strait closure; crude spikes. EU thermal dispatch forced; Libya ramp insufficient offset.

themes: Hormuz escalation premium pressuring thermal dispatch
GB power regime shift — extended strength vs EU
Storage deficit ahead of winter — refill pace critical
Libyan crude ramping offsets geopolitical upside
Data-center load growth structurally supporting power forwards
top_drivers: Hormuz geopolitical escalation raising crude and thermal fuel cost; TTF +4.2% on tail risk; Libya ramping provides mechanical offset.
GB power at 97th percentile (165.91 EUR/MWh) signals acute GB supply-side or demand regime shift vs EU; storage deficit (16.8 pp below seasonal) tightening winter forwards.
Data-center structural demand growth in EU (Google Austria, others) supporting power curve and reducing downside risk from demand destruction.
top_takeaway: GB power at 97th percentile, TTF +4.2% on Hormuz geopolitics, EU storage 16.8 pp below seasonal — thermal premium is entrenched; Libya offset provides upside relief.

watchlist.metric: Hormuz Strait closure or shipping incident
watchlist.why: Immediate crude spike triggers EU thermal dispatch upside; TTF already pricing 4–6% risk premium on geopolitical tail.
At 16.8 pp below seasonal, any LNG supply disruption or demand overshoot will force winter 2026-27 power curve higher; backstop for Cal+1 supports.

watchlist.metric: Libya crude export ramp to EU — volume & timing
watchlist.why: Offsetting mechanism for Hormuz premium; rising Libyan barrels lower marginal fuel cost and ease power upside relief, reducing geopolitical tail risk.

watchlist.metric: Norway Arctic drilling permit and FID timeline
watchlist.why: Gas supply continuity into 2027 reduces EU LNG import dependency; permit approval signals TTF downside structural relief vs spot scarcity pricing.

watchlist.metric: EU data-center load expansion — Google Austria capex/location decisions
watchlist.why: Structural demand growth into 2027 supports forward power curve; reduces deflationary pressure from demand destruction, raising peak-hour marginal value.
